question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 795 through 804 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.
family: THE FAMILY IS THE SAME FAULT IN THE SAME PLACE TWICE, AND THE ONLY THING THAT HAS CHANGED IS THAT THE PERSON NOW KNOWS EXACTLY HOW IT IS DONE. A job is found in a place where the same job has already been found. Somebody means to do it their own way and somebody else arrives and does the second half properly, and it is done properly again and it is the best repair in the chapter. The place is no better and no worse than it was. The person is different in exactly one respect, which is that they cannot go back to doing it the way they used to, and that is not a fault in them and there is nothing to be done about it. Every one of the ten jobs physically takes two people and no job in the ten can be finished by one. Nobody in any of the ten can use what they have learned.
family_why_this_and_not_the_nearest: 785 to 794 was A GOOD REPAIR AND WHAT THE PERSON DOES WITH IT AFTERWARDS, and the fault there was in the person undoing the value of a good repair. 795 to 804 is the direct inversion of it and the inversion is the whole point: the repair stays, the person stays, the place stays, nothing is undone by anybody, and what is different is that the person has watched the whole of a job done from the off and cannot do it and will not be able to do it and will not have anybody else who can. Nothing in this block is undone. Nothing in this block is refused. Nothing in this block is carried, told, brought, written, wrapped, stacked, counted, deferred, watered, rung at, or left standing at an edge.

0796 from the middle of the morning until the ground is too wet to stand in she is at the bottom of her own boundary at number ten, and four turns of wire round one post is the whole of what that day is about

0798 out in that yard at number twelve from the light coming up until she cannot stand in it, and the gate propped against that wall since September is the whole of what she is out there for
0799 she is out at the back of number nine for the whole of that day with the back door off its hinges, and the hand's width that door is out of line with itself is the whole of the job
0800 all of that Thursday goes on the air brick at the back of that unit and on the wall behind it, from first light to the last, and the damp coming up that wall is what it is about

0801 she is in her own yard and her own bay on that Sunday from the time the frost is off the ground until she cannot lift another one, and four pallets with the blocks wet through in the middle of them are the whole of it

0802 she is out in her own yard at number twelve for most of that Friday with a barrow and a shovel, and twenty barrowloads of the heap that has banked against that shed wall since the summer is the whole of it
0803 that whole Tuesday is spent in her own yard at number nine between the middle of the morning and the end of it, and the tub of iron that lives on the middle of her path is what it is about

0804 beginning about half way through the morning and going on until the light is going, she is in her own shed at number ten with the sack lying on its side, and the hole worn through the bottom of it is the whole of that day

cards.0795: At the unit a man in his early forties has a gate on two hinges that has to be lifted to be shut, and means to pack the hinge stile with wedges and screw it tight; the woman from two doors down takes the gate off its hinges on trestles, gets the stile back into square with a long diagonal brace bolted across two corners and let in so that it is part of the frame and not a stick on the front of it, hangs it back on new buttons so that it shuts with a hand's weight and not a shoulder, and it shuts; the gate is right and the gate is square and the latch is still hooked back over it because the staple on the frame is not done until April, and he has now watched the whole of a two-person job from the off and he cannot do any of it.
cards.0796: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has four turns of galvanised wire bitten into a post on a leaning run of close boarding and means to cut them off; her sister cuts them, takes the far post of that run out and gets the bottom rail back on the line of the rest of the run with the wire's own bright bites scarfed over and a new turn of wire put back on, and the run is better than it has been since she took the boarding up; and the woman in her yard now knows precisely how that is done and it is two people and a saw and she is one, and there is nobody on that boundary but her.
cards.0797: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a roller shutter that judders at the top because its track has been packing with grit since the autumn and means to clear the grit out; the woman who books work takes the shutter off its drum on a bar with two of them under it, cleans the drum and the whole of the track and puts it back, and the shutter runs up and down without a sound; and it is two people and a bar and a morning and she knows both halves of it.
cards.0798: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a gate propped back against a wall since September because it is a gate on a wall it does not close against, and means to have a catch put on it; her sister will not, and lets in a new hanging stile on the wall end, two new jamb hinges and a stop in the ground, and the gate is a gate and shuts and latches; and it is two people and a brace and a level and the old woman has watched all of it and cannot do any of it.
cards.0799: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a back door out of line with itself by a hand's width where it crosses a stone because it was hung too far closed in the autumn, and means to plane the bottom of it; the woman who does her shopping takes the door off its hinges, re-hangs it a hand's width higher on new longer keeps so that it shuts on its own frame and not on the stone, and it shuts; and it is two people and a door that weighs what it weighs, and she now knows exactly what has to be done to it and has nobody to do it with.
cards.0800: At the unit a man in his early forties has a damp patch coming up the wall behind a cowl on an air brick and means to patch the wall; the woman from two doors down will not, because the patch is not the fault and will keep coming until the air path is dealt with, and the job on the page is the cowl taken off, the plate made good where the air brick comes through, the cowl re-hung on a plate with a brace on the side of it and the face of the brick below it made good; the wall is dry to the shoulder by the summer and the fault is that he now knows what goes on the end of that pipe and cannot get at it.
cards.0801: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has four pallets standing on edge against a wall with a stack of blocks in the middle of every one of them wet through since June and means to turn them; the woman who books work has to take the whole four out into the yard to clear the wall, turn them the other way up and put them back with the blocks off the ground on bearers, and it is two people and a clear morning; and it is the third time that wall has been emptied and the woman who owns it now knows exactly how it is done and cannot lift a stack of blocks by herself at the end of a day.
cards.0802: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a heap of cut grass banked against her shed wall since the summer with a wet-tea stripe up the brick above it and means to take it down; her sister takes it down and moves it to the far end of that yard and spreads it about a foot deep over ground that has not had anything on it since before she came, and the stripe on the brick stops where it was and does not go further, because there is nothing behind it to go up; and it is twenty barrowloads and two people and the old woman has done the whole of it and knows exactly which barrowful goes where.
cards.0803: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a galvanised tub of iron standing on the middle of her front path because there is nowhere in that yard for it, and means to put it somewhere else; the woman who does her shopping takes it off the path, and there is nowhere to put it, and so there is a shelf, and she puts a shelf on the flat wall under the front window of that house, braced and screwed into sound brick and not into the sill, and the tub goes on it and off the path; and it is two people and a brace and four hours, and the flag she had taken up in January is back under a tub and she now knows exactly what goes on that wall.
cards.0804: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a sack lying on its side in her shed with a hole worn through the bottom of it about the size of a coin and half a bucket of topsoil banked up inside it, and means to tip the topsoil out; her sister says the sack is on its side because the bottom has gone and the topsoil is going through the hole as it stands, so the sack is turned out, the old bottom is cut away and a new one is sewn on with a needle and a hank of twine and the topsoil goes back in; and it is two people and a needle and a hank of twine, and the woman now knows how it is done and will be doing it on her own for the rest of her life.

movement: Ten jobs, ten good methods with no hole in any of them, ten repairs that stay repaired, and ten faults that are in nobody's method and nobody's hands. 0795 a gate taken off its hinges on trestles and squared with a bolted diagonal brace, and a man who has watched the whole of it. 0796 a boundary run opened and put true and its wire bites scarfed over, and a woman who knows it needs two people. 0797 a roller shutter off its drum and its track cleaned and it back on, and an owner who knows both halves. 0798 a gate on a wall made into a gate with a hanging stile and a stop in the ground, and a woman who watched it and could not do it. 0799 a back door re-hung a hand's width higher so that it shuts on its frame, and an owner who knows what has to be done to it. 0800 a cowl off, a plate made good and a brace on the side of a cowl, and the damp stopped at the shoulder, and a man who knows what goes on the end of that pipe. 0801 four pallets out of a bay and turned and put back on bearers, and an owner who cannot lift a stack of blocks at the end of a day. 0802 twenty barrowloads of a grass heap moved to ground that has not had anything on it, and an old woman who knows which barrowful goes where. 0803 a shelf braced into sound brick under a window and the tub lifted off the path, and an owner who knows exactly what goes on that wall. 0804 a new bottom sewn on a builder's sack with a needle and a hank of twine, and an owner who will be doing it on her own for the rest of her life. Every job is dry work and every job is done from the ground and every job takes two people.
closing_images: Ten different ones, and not one of the ten is a thing put away and not one is a thing left where it is. 0795 a square gate that shuts with a hand and a man in his own yard with a brace lying on the bench that he did not cut. 0796 a boundary run with its wire bites scarfed over and one person standing at the bottom of it. 0797 a shutter that runs without a sound and two bars where one was. 0798 a gate latched for the first time in a year with the old woman inside a shut gate that she could not make. 0799 a back door that shuts on its own frame and the stone offcut lying there doing nothing. 0800 a cowl braced on a new plate and a man with a brace he cannot get the end of in the right place with a bar. 0801 four pallets on edge the other way up on bearers and one person's back at the end of it. 0802 a heap spread a foot deep at the far end of a yard and the stripe on the brick stopped where it was. 0803 a shelf under a window with a tub of iron on it and a flag underneath it. 0804 a sack standing on its own bottom for the first time since May with a hank of twine and a needle beside it. THE DEPART-AND-DO-NOT-FOLLOW GESTURE IS IN 0798, 0801 AND 0804 ONLY. A DEPARTURE OUT OF A GATE IS IN 0796 AND 0802.

prohibitions_honoured.no_arithmetic_engine: Nothing is added up, nothing is priced, nothing is counted and no number is asked to agree with another. There is no figure-mismatch spread and no telephone. No tap is run and no water is drawn, carried, poured or emptied anywhere in the ten.
prohibitions_honoured.furniture: At most ordinary domestic pairs are used as furniture. No measurement, price, room tally or mismatch is the engine of any chapter.
prohibitions_honoured.standing_objects_untouched: The freeholder does not arrive. The line is not put right. The ladder is not opened and no room is painted. The box behind the lock-up bench is not opened and nothing is asserted about its lid either way, INCLUDING THE LINE IN 0785, WHICH IS A CONFLICT A HUMAN HAS NOT RULED ON. The drawer with leads and screws is not opened. The drawer at ten stays shut with the hammer, the screwdriver and the paper with three lines on it. The front room at number twelve is not entered. The report is not chased. The envelope is not turned. The bowl stays on its shelf and the ring on the tiles. No felt is nailed. No ply is nailed at number ten. The gate at twelve is no longer propped after 0798 and that is the job. The sash at twelve stays a hand's width low for good. The slab at nine stays tilting to the rail. THE STAPLE ON THE GATE FRAME AT THE UNIT IS NOT DONE AND NO CARD MAY STAND ON IT, THE LATCH STAYS HOOKED BACK OVER THE GATE, AND APRIL IS NOT ON THE PAGE. Nothing is carried between people and nothing is passed from one to another.
prohibitions_honoured.wet_jobs: NONE, AND THE TWO FLAGS THIS BLOCK INHERITS ARE THE ONLY TWO AND BOTH ARE A HUMAN'S: the cement bed in 0784 and the collar of old concrete broken off in 0787. A CARD THAT CANNOT BE WRITTEN WITHOUT A CEMENT BED MUST BE REWRITTEN BEFORE IT IS USED.
prohibitions_honoured.the_coal_hole_wood: In 0799 and 0803 the load standing in the coal hole is not looked into, not counted and not carried out, and the green furry middle from 0768 is not mentioned.
prohibitions_honoured.one_edge_one_visitor: One visitor at one edge per chapter at most in all ten. No chapter has a second visitor and no chapter has a visitor at two edges.

still_live_and_taken_up_by_nobody_here: Four pallets with bearers under them and the wall they came off empty again. The shutter and its track. The near gate square with a brace in it. A gate on a wall that is a gate. A back door shut on its frame. A cowl braced on a plate and the damp stopped at the shoulder. A boundary run with scarfed bites in the post. A heap of grass on ground that has not had anything on it. A shelf under a window with a tub on it. A sack with a new bottom. Off the page and waiting on the man off the ring road, who has now sat out five blocks: a figure for four rooms given aloud twice in a lock-up and written nowhere; a frame out of square which its own man will find at the fitting; a landing wall with a bare patch on it and a mirror in a van; a fourth room at the top of a stair that nobody has priced or looked into. Three lines of paper shut in a drawer on purpose with the tools that would do them. A box in a corner of a lock-up whose lid is not nailed.

read_back.readers: One second reader, run over the ten finished chapters with eight canon chapters (0785 to 0791 and 0794) and sixteen points, arithmetic and facts first and prose last. It returned forty findings. Thirty-eight were fixed in the prose and two are recorded below as not a writer's to settle.
the_two_that_were_the_method_and_worth_t: 0797's bars could not do what the chapter needed them to do. The first draft lifted a curtain clear of its side guides on two bars stood on end, which no roller shutter can do, and then cleaned six feet of a guide that was still full of curtain. It is now the bottom rail that comes up out of the guide channels on two bars, which is what the bars are for and which is done every week on a shutter like that; the bottom of each guide is cleaned from the floor, and the drum and the mouth of the housing are cleaned with a rag on the end of a length of tube from the curb, and it runs without a sound.

0803's brace was in the plane of the wall, so it could not have resisted the arm of the bracket rotating out of it. It now goes from the outer end of the arm, on the underside of it, back and down into a joint below. 0800's cowl brace had the same fault and is now a strut under the front of the cowl back and down into the joint below the air brick.
the_others_that_were_a_fact_and_not_a_wo: 0803 carried three paragraphs of a writer thinking, including a staging and a withdrawal of an assertion about the frozen front gate; they are cut and replaced with the tub coming off the bed and going four feet along the path.

0800 credited the lock-up's cleaned shutter to the unit's own door and to the wrong woman.
0802 gave number twelve a shed felt, which belongs to number ten and is a live unresolved object there.
0799 called the visitor her sister, which is the tradeswoman at ten and twelve.
0799 narrated the writing process twice, once in a clause and once in the body.
0803 put the woman of the house inside her own front room, which stays shut.
0796 put eleven feet of close boarding down on its own two ends with the far post out of the ground.

the_two_taken_as_findings_against_the_bl: The all-caps card paragraph at the head of each chapter, which has run for hundreds of chapters and is a human's decision.
The conflict between canon 0793, which leaves the coal hole lid off in the wet at nine, and this block's standing, which has it shut. 0799 and 0803 say shut and are not edited.
read_back.what_the_reader_called_the_weakest_thing: THE CLOSING FORMULA. 'She can say exactly' was in seven of the ten and 'it is two people and two tools and she is one' was in five, and all ten ended on the same note. That is a template and not a family. It is now in none of the ten: the ten endings are a square gate that comes home with a hand, a post with four scars in it, two bars where there was one, a latch that drops into a keep, a door standing against a wall with new keeps in it, the end of a bar and the rest of the morning, bearers in the sun and a morning she will have to wait for, a stripe on a brick that stops where it was, four hours and nobody to take the other end of a bar, and a sack that stands on its own bottom and the one after it that will not.
